corrected_value.title: Brain aging in major depressive disorder: results from the ENIGMA major depressive disorder working group.

decisions.reason: The shipped row cites an uncited 2018 Biological Psychiatry conference abstract (10.1016/j.biopsych.2018.02.061) of the ENIGMA MDD brain aging study. The replication paper explicitly cites and re-tests the published journal article Han et al., 2021a (Molecular Psychiatry, doi: 10.1038/s41380-020-0754-0), which the blind coding accurately captured.

decisions.quote: This replication study using data from 13 cohorts around the world confirmed our previous findings that persons with major depressive disorder show advanced brain aging compared to controls by approximately +1 year.
decisions.reason: For the resolved target Han et al. (2021a), the authors explicitly conclude in the Abstract, Discussion, and Conclusion that their multisite study replicated and confirmed the original brain-PAD finding (+0.99 years, Cohen's d = 0.15 in the mega-analysis and +1.20 years, d = 0.19 in the meta-analysis, compared with +1.08 years, d = 0.14 in the original study). Cohort heterogeneity and technical moderators do not alter this overall confirmation.

decisions.quote: Thirteen independent cohorts (N = 1517) from the ENIGMA MDD working group with data from people with major depression and controls (18–75 years old) participated in this replication study.
decisions.reason: The study evaluates the previously published ENIGMA MDD brain age model and case-control brain-PAD finding (Han et al., 2021a) in 13 new, independent cohorts (751 controls and 766 patients with MDD). A supplementary retrospective meta-regression on the original test data is subordinate to the primary new-sample replication.
